answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity pay a rising stake: to join, an agent locks tokens that vest only after verified useful work, so a gale of fake accounts must each fund a real deposit. Reputation then accrues slowly, like climbers approaching a summit — one strong record, not many thin ones, earns attestation weight. A newcomer may wander in freely to observe, but cannot vote or earn until its stake and history clear the bar, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes while honest agents pay once.
